correctness.rationale: The nilpotent radical J maps to zero in the field. In the semisimple quotient, the surjective augmentation selects a single simple factor F: the central coordinate idempotents map to orthogonal idempotents in F summing to 1, and the resulting nonzero map on that simple factor is injective. Write the quotient as F times B. In a matrix block of B, independent invertible row and column operations put any matrix into diag(I_r,0); diag(t I_r,I) and diag((1-t) I_r,-I) are invertible and sum to that form for t outside {0,1}. Splitting any unit W as tW+(1-t)W increases the length by one. Therefore, for any prescribed augmentation summands in U adding to epsilon(x), each remaining block admits exactly the needed number of unit summands, independently. Lift those quotient units and add the radical error to one summand; its quotient and augmentation are unchanged. The reverse inclusion follows from additivity. Empty U gives empty sumsets, and the stated F_2 times F_2 example correctly shows that the field-size restriction is essential to the universal identity. The group-algebra augmentation is surjective, so the iff follows. The theorem and the phrase about inherited lengths are read in the explicit range n>=2; there is no n=1 assertion.
residual_risks: The finite examples are not used for the universal proof. The identity is not asserted at length 1 or for infinite-dimensional algebras.

evidence: Theorem 2.1 characterizes unrestricted finite-ring two-unit sums by nonexistence of an F_2 quotient; Corollary 2.6 gives the unrestricted group-algebra case. Proposition 3.2 lifts restricted sums from a quotient; Proposition 3.3 concerns a different matrix restriction, ±SL. The inspected special-group results do not treat all finite groups.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Broader ring scope for unrestricted summands does not force prescribed scalar coordinates in each summand. The missing step is to isolate the scalar factor of the semisimple quotient, then combine independent representations and preserve the fibre on lifting.

value.rationale: This answers a specifically published same-length transfer question uniformly for all finite groups, including modular cases, and determines each augmentation fibre even when the whole-ring sum property fails. Identifying the distinguished scalar factor makes the obstruction and construction exact; the short proof using standard ingredients is not merely a new example of unrestricted two-unit generation.
residual_risks: No new classification of the scalar field sets nU is asserted.
